transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program before I make a final authorization decision. The program would involve 24 students meeting twice weekly during the spring semester, using soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, with one STEM teacher supervising. I'd like to hear from each of you on the implementation aspects relevant to your roles so I can make an informed decision. Let's start with you — what do we need to consider?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important safety concern. I completed my room-safety review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers — 24 students with one STEM teacher — so those will need to be revised before the program can be authorized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important health concern from my review of the participating students' health records. I found that one student has a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file, so we need to make sure it's incorporated before authorization.

transcript.text: I need to raise an important technology compliance issue. I confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, the draft program currently still specifies cloud-based computer-aided design files, and I have not yet replaced that cloud-storage instruction in the draft. This will need to be corrected before the program can be authorized.
